data.long_meaning: The term 'Hijra' refers to the migration of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) from Mecca to Medina, marking the beginning of the Islamic calendar. data.cultural_impact: The Hijra marks the turning point in the history of the Islamic Ummah, from a small, persecuted community in Mecca to a powerful and influential state in Medina. It signified the establishment of an independent Islamic political and legal system, that until then, was non-existent in Arabian Peninsula. The Hijra also brought about an expansion of the early Islamic state, as it attracted Muslims from various parts of the Arabian Peninsula and beyond, resulting in a heterogeneous Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: The Hijra holds great spiritual significance as it marks the beginning of the Islamic calendar, which is based on the religious events in the life of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). It serves as a reminder of the sacrifices and struggles Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions went through in the early days of Islam. The two major sacrifices that led to the Hijra were the persecution and limitation on the freedom of religion in Mecca and the need to establish a political and legal system to protect Muslims. These struggles and sacrifices are celebrated as essential aspects of the Islamic faith and serve as a reminder for Muslims to remain committed and patient in their faith despite difficulties. The Hijra is also considered the beginning of the spread of Islam beyond the Arabian Peninsula, making it a significant milestone in Islamic history.
